title: Belt Drive Speed Calculator
description: The learner types the fan speed and belt count for four illustrative V-belt fan drives and gets the worked calculation back, then explores how sheave sizes, motor speed, service factor and per-belt rating change fan speed, belt speed and belt count.
creator: Twin City Fan

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Belt drives: fan speed, belt speed and belt count
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the fan speed, belt speed and required belt count of a V-belt fan drive from the motor speed, the two sheave pitch diameters, the motor horsepower and the drive service factor, with fan speed within ±5 rpm and belt count exact.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge; every slider is labelled and moves with the arrow keys; sheave rotation stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

controls.label: Rating per belt
controls.purpose: 1.0 to 20.0 hp per belt, step 0.5 (Explore mode)

equations: fan rpm = motor rpm × motor sheave ÷ fan sheave
belt speed (ft/min) = π × motor sheave (in) × motor rpm ÷ 12
design hp = motor hp × drive service factor
belts = ceiling(design hp ÷ rating per belt); a whole-number quotient is not rounded up
rules: Fan rpm is correct when |entered − model| ≤ 5 rpm; belt count is correct only when equal
The two answers are judged separately; a challenge is fully correct when both are right
Belt speed above 6,500 ft/min shows a note to check the drive manufacturer's limits
limitations: Motor speeds, per-belt ratings and service factors are illustrative; real selections use the drive manufacturer's current tables

sources: Chapter 11 "Sheave", "V-Belt" and "Drive Service Factor" sections; motor service factor contrast from FanPedia p. 69

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit two numbers per drive, get the worked calculation as feedback, then explore the inverse diameter relationship with sliders
keyQuestions: How fast will the fan turn, and how many belts does this drive need?
commonMisconceptions: A larger fan sheave makes the fan run faster
The speed ratio equals the diameter ratio the same way up (fan/motor)
A belt count of 3.25 rounds down to 3
The motor's nameplate service factor is the drive service factor
assessmentOpportunities: Running line 'Challenges fully correct: n of 4'; mastery is 4 of 4 drives with both answers right on the first attempt.
